name: Gran Melia Colon
positioning: Hotel Colón Gran Meliá: a 5-star hotel in a neoclassical building under a modernist dome, opened for the 1929 Universal Exposition, a few steps from Seville Cathedral
best_for: Travelers who want a central Seville base a few steps from the cathedral
Guests curious about Seville's bullfighting traditions

facts.text: The hotel opened for the 1929 Universal Exposition.
The hotel is in a neoclassical building under a modernist dome that is the heart of the hotel.
The hotel is a member of The Leading Hotels of the World.
The hotel is a few steps from main attractions such as the cathedral.
Deluxe Rooms are decorated by renowned interior designers such as Philippe Starck or Marcel Wanders.
El Burladero serves traditional Seville tapas such as salmorejo and oxtail.
The Spa by Clarins has a sauna, Turkish bath and contrast shower.
RedLevel guests have a butler available 24/7.
The Dehesa Majavieja experience visits the estate of bullfighter Espartaco to see fighting bulls in their habitat.

highlights.text: Colón Grand Café sits under the 1929 dome, with glass windows that tint the light.
The Penthouse Suite RedLevel has a terrace with an outdoor bathtub and panoramic views of the city.
El Burladero is a bullfighting-inspired restaurant serving dishes from traditional Sevillian recipes and local products.
The hotel runs a pet program for dogs with no weight limit and up to 2 pets per room.

considerations.text: The hotel is 12 km from the airport.
The spa's pool is a heated boutique pool, alongside a solarium terrace with sunbeds.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the hotel's luxury positioning.
